question: Should OpenClaw adopt this gateway-independent core architecture RFC as the target direction, keep it in draft for revision, or reject the proposed runtime ownership split?
rationale: The PR is a broad draft RFC; code review can check process and consistency, but cannot decide whether maintainers want this runtime and product boundary.

options.title: Keep Draft For Discussion
options.body: Leave the PR open in draft while maintainers use the required maintainer-discussion thread to revise scope, rollout gates, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Accept The RFC
options.body: Move the RFC toward accepted status and create the implementation issue once maintainers agree this is the target architecture.

options.title: Reject Or Replace Direction
options.body: Close or supersede the RFC if maintainers prefer the gateway-owned runtime model or a narrower proposal.

recommendation.title: Keep Draft For Discussion
recommendation.body: Leave the PR open in draft while maintainers use the required maintainer-discussion thread to revise scope, rollout gates, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: Kevin authored the RFC process/template commits that define how draft RFCs move through discussion and acceptance.
